chunks: And ʿAbdullāh ibn Bukayr narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام that he said:
“Indeed, I take a dirham from one of you, while I am surely among the wealthiest people of al-Madīnah in property. I intend by that nothing except that you may be purified.”

key_terms.أَكْثَرِ: among the wealthiest or most abundant in wealth
key_terms.الدِّرْهَمَ: a dirham; a unit of money taken from believers
key_terms.الْمَدِينَةِ: al-Madīnah, the city referenced in the report
key_terms.تُطَهَّرُوا: that you may be purified; spiritually cleansed through giving

ai.seo_question: Why does Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام say he takes a dirham from people despite not needing their wealth?
ai.summary: This hadith explains that the Imam عليه السلام did not take wealth out of personal need, despite being among the wealthiest people of al-Madīnah. Rather, taking it served a purifying function for the believers, indicating the spiritual significance of financial obligations such as khums.
